root_cause.text: The CXL mailbox user-input validation function `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` in `drivers/cxl/core/mbox.c` dereferenced and type-cast the raw payload before checking its length, allowing undersized ioctl payloads to trigger out-of-bounds reads in opcode-specific parsing such as `uuid_equal()` for `CXL_MBOX_OP_CLEAR_LOG`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() casts and dereferences the input payload without first verifying its size`, and adds `in_size` checks before accessing `struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info` and `uuid_t` (`if (in_size < sizeof(*pi)) return false;` / `if (in_size < sizeof(uuid_t)) return false;`), matching the reported KASAN read past the buffer in `uuid_equal()` from `drivers/cxl/core/mbox.c:345`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the in_size parameter in the cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() comment.
intent_record.what: A kernel-doc comment for cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() was updated to add a new parameter description line for @in_size, specifying it as the size of @payload_in in bytes.
intent_record.how: This change only affects the function's documentation and does not alter runtime behavior, control flow, or validation logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size check for the SET_PARTITION_INFO mailbox payload to reject undersized user input.
intent_record.what: The function `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` was changed to take an additional `size_t in_size` argument, and in the `CXL_MBOX_OP_SET_PARTITION_INFO` case it now checks `if (in_size < sizeof(*pi)) return false;` before accessing fields in the user-provided payload.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now verifies that the incoming payload buffer is large enough to contain a full `struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info` before dereferencing it, preventing out-of-bounds access or interpretation of undersized input for that opcode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size check to reject undersized Clear Log payloads before accessing the UUID.
intent_record.what: In cxl_payload_from_user_allowed(), inside the CXL_MBOX_OP_CLEAR_LOG case, two lines were added to check whether in_size is smaller than sizeof(uuid_t) and immediately return false if so.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from treating an undersized user-provided payload as a valid UUID payload, avoiding out-of-bounds access or misinterpretation when handling the Clear Log mailbox command.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the input payload size into the CXL mailbox permission check so payload validation can be performed correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to `cxl_payload_from_user_allowed()` in `cxl_mbox_cmd_ctor()` was changed to pass an additional `in_size` argument, and the function call was reformatted across two lines.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the input-payload अनुमति check now has access to the requested input size, so validation can make a decision based on both the opcode and the payload length instead of only the payload pointer/object. This can prevent accepting or rejecting mailbox inputs incorrectly when size matters.

The fix targets the SET_PARTITION_INFO mailbox payload size check, while the root cause is the generic user-payload validation in cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() that allowed undersized ioctl inputs to be dereferenced before length checks, affecting opcode-specific parsing like CLEAR_LOG.
The change directly addresses the reported root cause by adding a length check for Clear Log payloads before the UUID is accessed, preventing the undersized-payload out-of-bounds read.

The change directly addresses the root cause by passing the payload size into the CXL mailbox validation path, which is needed to validate ioctl payload length before opcode-specific parsing and avoid out-of-bounds reads.

candidates.rationale: This casts the raw user-controlled payload buffer to a UUID pointer before any size validation. For undersized CLEAR_LOG ioctls, later UUID access can read past the end of the buffer, which matches the root cause.

This is the permission-check call that, in the buggy version, did not receive the payload length. Because validation was done without size information, opcode-specific parsing could dereference undersized input and trigger out-of-bounds reads.
